payload.pattern_description: Under-threshold burst: 4 online purchases each between $450 and $499.99 ($1,906.07 in total) inside 30 minutes on a card with almost no online history, split across 2 New device profiles and 2 purchaser email domains. Amounts sit just under a $500 authorisation threshold. 12 other cards show the identical shape within 30 days (C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C03633-K1, C05423-K1, C05766-K1, C05851-K1, C06208-K1, C06881-K1, C10751-K1, C10990-K1, C12641-K2); five closed cases with this shape were confirmed as undocumented fraud and reported.

assessment.calibration_basis: p_engine is 0.90, set by the scorecard's denial+burst floor adjustment (0.9) over cal_p 0.0117 / cms_p 0.0126; the harness applies this floor because in this data no customer denial has ever been cleared and the flagged transaction sits inside the seeded just-under-$500 online burst (episode 3476602/3476633/3476665/3476682). I keep fraud_probability at the floor value of 0.90 rather than moving further: the customer denial (source customer, ref trigger) and the burst shape are two independent, strong evidence families that already meet the §6 stop test, and the low cms_p/risk_score on these transactions is exactly the kind of under-scored undocumented pattern the floor exists to correct, not a reason to discount it.

evidence.claim: Customer C07297 states they never made the $482.12 purchase 3476682; in this bank's closed-case history 0 of the customer-reported denials were ultimately cleared, so the denial alone floors the case above the verify-first threshold.

under_threshold_burst found the flagged transaction inside a 4-member online burst on card C07297-K1 (3476602 $478.95, 3476633 $456.96, 3476665 $488.04, 3476682 $482.12), all between 20:00 and 20:30 on 2016-11-21, all product code C, using two New device profiles (Trident/IE11/Windows7 and iOS Safari) and two purchaser email domains (gmail.com, yahoo.com); this matches the just-under-$500 undocumented burst shape.

As of opening the card had 199 prior transactions (card_seq 200 minus 1) with a prior median amount of $62.93 and a prior maximum of $1,104, and only 6 online transactions in its whole history, so the $1,906.07 online burst is a sharp break from the card's baseline.

under_threshold_burst also lists 12 other cards (C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C03633-K1, C05423-K1, C05766-K1, C05851-K1, C06208-K1, C06881-K1, C10751-K1, C10990-K1, C12641-K2) showing the same just-under-$500 shape within 30 days, indicating coordinated repeated abuse rather than a one-off.

find_similar_cases returned four closed cases confirmed as fraud on the same generic device profiles (CC-3368, CC-5111, CC-3624, CC-1476), three labeled card_not_present_new_device and one card_not_present_fraud, reinforcing that New-device online bursts of this size on this card population have previously been confirmed fraudulent.

evidence.claim: The calibrated case-memory score (cms_p) on the flagged transaction is 0.0126 and the real-time risk_score is 0.25, both low, so the model component alone leans legitimate and conflicts with the denial and burst signals.

recurring_charge_check found only 1 matching prior instance for this amount/place (gmail.com), far short of the 5 needed for the R7 recurring-charge exception, so the disputed charge does not match an established recurring pattern and R7 does not apply.

shared_origin_scan shows both burst device profiles are generic rather than exclusive: the Trident/IE11 profile appears on 359 cards and the iOS Safari profile on 354 cards in the 30 days before opening, so neither qualifies as a strong shared-origin (R6) device and no connected cards/profiles are named.

assessment.pattern_description: This is the just-under-$500 online burst shape: four product-C online purchases of $478.95, $456.96, $488.04 and $482.12 (summing to $1,906.07) placed within 30 minutes on 2016-11-21, split across two New device profiles and two purchaser email domains, all priced just below a likely $500 authorization threshold. It affects a card that is almost entirely in-person (only 6 online transactions in its whole prior history) and was found via under_threshold_burst, which also lists 12 other cards showing the identical shape within the same 30-day window. Several closed cases with this exact shape were confirmed as fraud and reported, which is why it is treated as a coordinated, undocumented abuse pattern rather than an isolated bad purchase.

actions.reason: 3a: exposure $1,906.07 > $1,000 and the pattern is undocumented (just-under-$500 burst), and R2: the customer denied transaction 3476682, so a case is opened to hold the episode.
R2: customer denied transaction 3476682 and exposure $1,906.07 ≤ $2,500, so blocking this card is recommended pending team-lead approval.
3a/R9: exposure $1,906.07 > $1,000 and the undocumented just-under-$500 burst shape recurs on 12 other cards in the same 30-day window, so a report is recommended pending fraud-manager approval.
R9: the episode fits no documented pattern but shows coordinated, repeated abuse across customers (the just-under-$500 burst shared by 12 lookalike cards), so an analyst should review the wider wave.
